t:
(a) 
Strategic Plan for Science and Engineering Education.—Section 107 of the Education for Economic Security Act (20 U.S.C. 3917) is repealed.
 
    (b) 
Budget Estimate.—Section 14 of the National Science Foundation Act of 1950 (42 U.S.C. 1873) is amended by striking subsection (j).

fable.w: The section only repeals a strategic-plan provision and strikes a budget-estimate subsection. The tempting reading is that a "Strategic Plan" heading implies consultation with outside parties, but the text creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, rulemaking authority, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: Section 107 of the Education for Economic Security Act (20 U.S.C. 3917) is repealed.

opus.w: This section only repeals one statutory provision and strikes a subsection of another. Nothing in the text involves parties outside the federal government in a federal decision. Reading participation into it would mean guessing at what the repealed provisions said, and the text itself contains no consultation, hearing, comment, advisory, or litigation mechanism.
opus.s: Section 107 of the Education for Economic Security Act (20 U.S.C. 3917) is repealed.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through:** One could read the repeal of a science and engineering education "Strategic Plan" provision as touching on a planning process that once involved outside consultation. That reading fails. The section only repeals one provision and strikes another. It does not create, require, or authorize any consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue, and no one outside the federal government is involved.

qwen_chat.w: The section consists entirely of legislative instructions to repeal and amend other statutes. It does not establish any process for consulting with or coordinating with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory committees, public hearings, comment periods, or rights to sue mentioned.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that repealing a section or amending a budget estimate implies some form of public input or consultation, but the text itself contains no such requirement. It is purely a legislative amendment instruction.
